RagShortTexts: Ancient Venedi references do not establish a unified Venedians state in 374.
River access, exchange and the burden of protection shape this scenario's local disputes.

Variants.Content: Venedians is the module's label for a playable group, not proof that ancient references to Venedi describe one coherent state in 374. Names used by outside writers do not supply a complete account of local identity or government. The faction's disputes can concern river travel, exchange, relations with neighbouring peoples and how settlements support armed protection. A leader who obtains useful contacts may still face opposition over the cost. This approach preserves the scenario while avoiding fabricated senatorial houses, five hereditary castles or a later national monarchy imposed upon poorly documented communities.

A guard beside a river landing needs warning from the next settlement and a clear signal before letting strangers approach. Families depend on the same route for trade, so closing it also costs food and work. The armed men must explain a precaution to the people supplying them, rather than treat every question as disloyalty.

A Venedi notable may gain standing by arranging passage or exchange with a neighbour, but cannot promise goods he does not control. The families bearing the burden will remember a broken pledge. His position rests on recognised relationships in this scenario, not on a supposedly documented hereditary office for all ancient Venedi.
